body:
Here's your Friday morning brief for Kern County:

Good morning, Bakersfield. It's Friday, August 28th, and our top story this morning is a look at how Bakersfield College's industrial automation program has grown over the past decade to meet local workforce needs. We're starting the day at 84 degrees at Meadows Field with partly sunny skies expected, and no weather alerts active. Overnight, crews handled a grass fire near the freeway and several medical calls across the county.

## The Kern Overnight

Overnight activity across Kern County was moderate, with a grass fire, a possible overdose, a domestic disturbance, a rooftop welfare check and several medical calls keeping responders busy. Around 10:55 p.m., fire crews and a battalion chief were sent to the area of the Hampton Inn on East Brundage Lane near the freeway for a reported grass fire. Shortly after 4 a.m., medical crews were called to the front of Brookside on Coffee Road, where a person outside at the tables was unconscious but breathing in what was reported as a possible overdose. Just after 11 p.m., officers responded to an apartment on Lincoln Street for a domestic disturbance in which a woman reported being prevented from leaving. About 11:30 p.m., deputies checked on a Grand Prairie Drive home after the resident reported their alarm sounding and said someone was on the roof. Overnight calls also included a diabetic emergency on West Mariposa Avenue and a check on a vehicle passenger near Wofford Heights.

## Today's weather

Expect a high near 96° and a low around 70° tonight. It's currently 84° at Meadows Field (KBFL). No active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is currently n/a and there are no active fires reported in the county.

## Top stories

**KGET 17 reports that** week 2 of the high school football season is underway across Bakersfield and Kern County, with local teams taking to the field for their latest matchups. The station will have scores and highlights from the games as they come in throughout the evening.

**23ABC tells us that** Bakersfield College's industrial automation program has grown significantly since its launch a decade ago, from just seven graduates in its first class to 34 this year. The program was created to address a local workforce shortage in technical skills, and now boasts a 98% job-placement rate among graduates seeking work. Professor Roy Allard said the program's success is due to strong industry partnerships and a focus on hands-on training that prepares students for the workforce.

**According to KGET 17,** a Kern County World War II veteran recently celebrated his 102nd birthday. The station shared the remarkable milestone, highlighting the long and impactful life of a local resident who has contributed to our community and nation.

**23ABC said that** the Renegades football team carries a century of championship tradition into their highly anticipated Saturday matchup. Players and coaches say they feel the weight of that legacy as they prepare to take the field, with running back Austin Hernandez noting that the support of longtime fans drives his motivation on the field.

**23ABC announced that** CSUB has named a new head coach for its women's basketball team. Ray Alvarado, who spent last season as associate head coach and interim head coach this spring, will now take the reins permanently. Alvarado said he wants to bring stability, leadership and a strong culture to the program, with a focus on recruiting local talent from the Central Valley.

**Bakersfield Now reports that** three people are dead and several others injured after a crash on Copus Road. The outlet said emergency crews responded to the scene of the collision, which involved multiple vehicles and required a hazardous materials response due to a fuel leak. The road was closed for several hours while investigators worked to determine the cause of the crash.

## Something good

Kern County WWII veteran celebrates 102nd birthday. This remarkable milestone highlights the long and impactful life of a local resident who has contributed to our community and nation.

## Coming up this week

Looking ahead, several public meetings and events are on the calendar for the coming days. On Wednesday, September 2nd at 12:00 p.m., the Personnel and Processes Committee will meet. Also on Wednesday at 8:30 a.m., the Police Civil Service Commission will convene. Then on Thursday, September 3rd at 5:30 p.m., the Planning Commission will hold its meeting.

On the entertainment front, the Fox Theater has several shows coming up. Tonight, Friday August 28th, catch CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE. Then on Saturday August 29th, comedian Willie Barcena takes the stage, followed by Danny ELBC Presents: Michael Return Of The King Tribute later that evening. Looking ahead to next week, on Thursday September 3rd, the theater will host both the MI HISTORIA TOUR LEYENDAS DEL MARIACHI USA and The Oldies Night: A Night Of Timeless Soul, Doo-Wop, & Classic Oldies.
